$comment: The items of an input and how each stands (roadmap phase N, decisions D62 and D63, accepted 2026-09-21). An item is a run of digits (`182`, `1,000` with its separators), an ordinal (`9th`), or one of the symbols below; `!` and `?` are items only inside a word, where they are characters rather than marks. Under the literal rule nothing is converted: a number is never read as its name and a symbol never as a letter. Until the literal phase (N3) counts digits and symbols as characters of the pool, every item is left out and the line under the field says so, which is `drop`, the one reading this table offers; N3 adds `self` and the leet readings here. `scripts/gen-readings.py` emits this table into crates/anagram-core/src/readings_table.rs and packages/engine/src/readingsTable.ts; the item finder is written by hand on each side (readings.rs, readings.ts) and held to the `cases` below by a test on each side. Edit this file, then run the generator.
